name: add-food-definition
description: Use when the user names a food to add, asks to add a food entry, or wants a new food written into samples/definitions-food.json from the Import food nutrition prompt.
purpose: Add one or more named foods to samples/definitions-food.json. Nutrition objects follow the Import food definition prompt builder (Have AI help me), then get appended to the sample file.
onInvoke: The user named a food (or a list of foods) to add to the sample food definitions. You fill the Import food prompt yourself and append the objects. Do not stop after drafting a prompt for ChatGPT.
If they did not name a food, ask which food. Do not invent a food.

If they already named a portion, use that portion. If they did not, follow the serving rules below and write the entry. Ask only when the name is a different food under two reasonable readings (which brand, which recipe), not when only the household serving is unspecified.

files.ui: Import food definition modal → ✨ Have AI help me (#import-ai-panel, #import-ai-portion)

readBeforeWriting: Read buildAiPromptFromPortion, jsonSchemaExample, and nutrientListForPrompt in app.js before estimating nutrients.
Keys, labels, and units come from those functions. If this skill and app.js disagree, app.js wins.
jsonSchemaExample() zeroes every key as a shape demo. Those zeroes are not data. Do not paste that object into the file.
rulesFromBuilder: Return JSON matching the structure: one object, or an array when there is more than one common serving. Omit any nutrient key you cannot estimate.
Use the portion in the name field.

If the food is missing serving information, append a common serving size to the end of the food name (e.g. 1/2 cup, 1 cup, 1 oz, 2 oz, 3 oz). Prefer everyday portions people actually log. If the serving is in oz, add a visual reference in parentheses if possible (e.g. "3 oz (palm-sized)", "1 oz (about a small handful)"). If it's usually eaten all in one sitting from a container or bag, name it as container or bag followed by oz etc in parenthesis.

If the food has more than one common serving size people actually log, return an array of objects — one object per serving — with all nutrients scaled to that serving. When the user already named one portion, write only that portion.
Amounts for the micro requirements panel belong in micros. When the same nutrient key also appears in longevity, store the number in micros only and set longevity[key] to true.

If the food is a multivitamin or vitamin entry: Don't just list the label DV. Adjust both the DV and actual values for typical absorption, since we don't absorb 100% of a pill for every vitamin. If there is fat soluble vitamins, assume enough fats were eaten to absorb the fat-soluble vitamins (A, D, E, K).

required.name: Non-empty string. Food, then the serving at the end, matching existing names such as "Lamb steak 3 oz (palm-sized)". Keep the user's wording when it already includes a serving.

optional.micros: object of numeric amounts. Units are whatever nutrientListForPrompt assigns to that key.
optional.longevity: object. Longevity-only keys are numbers. Keys that also exist in micros are boolean true.
optional.carbQuality: object. glycemicIndex (GI, not grams), addedSugar (g), refinedCarbs (g). Also set netCarbs (g) to carbs minus fiber when fiber is known; the file stores it even though CARB_QUALITY_KEYS does not list it.
optional.notes: string. Cite the published source, the gram weight scaled to, and any important omission. The prompt schema omits notes; the sample file includes them.

values: Scale every number to the serving in the name.
Use a published source: USDA FoodData Central, a national food table (CoFID or equivalent), or the product label for a branded food. Name that source in notes.
Omit keys the source does not report. A stored 0 means the source reported zero, or the nutrient is absent for that food (vitamin B12 in an unfortified plant food, vitamin C in unfortified oil).
Do not copy the zero-filled schema. Do not invent a full micronutrient panel to look complete.
Protein, carbs, and fats are required. If you cannot find those three, do not append the food; say what source you checked.
Only use micros, longevity, and carbQuality keys that jsonSchemaExample / nutrientListForPrompt emit, plus carbQuality.netCarbs and notes.
workflow: Search samples/definitions-food.json for the food name (case-insensitive). Use search; do not load the whole file.
If the same food and the same serving already exist, report the existing name and stop. Do not add a second copy. A different serving of the same food is allowed when it is not already there.
Read the three prompt-builder functions in app.js. Estimate nutrients using their rules and units.
Build one object per serving you are adding.
Append those objects to the end of the JSON array. Put a comma after the previous last object. Match the file's 2-space indent. Do not re-serialize or reformat the rest of the file.
Validate, then tell the user each new name, its serving, and the source in notes.

duplicateCheck.search: Grep samples/definitions-food.json for the food words and for "name" lines.
duplicateCheck.sameServing: Stop and report the existing name.
duplicateCheck.differentServing: Append only the new serving, scaled on its own.
duplicateCheck.userNamedPortion: One object for that portion, even if other servings are also common.

also: The file must still be a JSON array.
Each name you just added appears once, and that object has numeric protein, carbs, and fats.
The file already contains a few repeated names. Do not treat those as a reason to reformat the file. Do not add another copy of a name that is already present.

doNot: Do not write the entry only in the chat.
Do not edit definitions-food-categories.json in this skill. If the new name is likely uncategorized, say so. Categorizing is the categorize-food-definitions skill.
Do not change existing food objects.
Do not put a bridge nutrient's number in longevity. The number stays in micros; longevity gets true.
Do not add foods the user did not name.
